question: What is the execution model of a MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline? What is the execution model of a MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline?

options.text: A multi-stage streaming pipeline where documents pass sequentially through transformation operators ($match, $unwind, $group, $sort).
A single monolithic query compiled once into a query plan, where all stages ($match, $group, $sort) execute simultaneously against the whole collection in parallel.
Each stage in the pipeline runs to completion and materializes its full output to a temporary collection on disk before the next stage begins reading it.
The pipeline evaluates stages in reverse order, starting from the final $sort or $group stage and working backward to determine which documents $match needs to fetch.

explanation: Specification answer: A multi-stage streaming pipeline where documents pass sequentially through transformation operators ($match, $unwind, $group, $sort).

question: How does the $lookup stage perform left outer joins between collections? How does the $lookup stage perform left outer joins between collections?

options.text: It matches localField in the source collection to foreignField in the target collection, outputting matches as an embedded array.
It matches documents whose _id in the source collection equals any field in the target collection, replacing the source document's fields with the matched target document's fields.
It performs an inner join by default, only including source documents that have at least one match in the target collection, and drops any source document without a match.
It requires both collections to be sharded on the same key so the join can be computed independently on each shard without any data movement.

explanation: Specification answer: It matches localField in the source collection to foreignField in the target collection, outputting matches as an embedded array.

question: What is the difference between a Targeted Query and a Scatter-Gather Query in a sharded cluster? What is the difference between a Targeted Query and a Scatter-Gather Query in a sharded cluster?

options.text: Targeted queries include the Shard Key and route to exactly 1 shard; Scatter-Gather queries lack the shard key and broadcast to every shard in the cluster.
A Targeted Query is any query the application marks with a targeted: true flag; mongos does not actually inspect the filter to decide routing.
Scatter-Gather queries are always faster than Targeted queries for point lookups, because querying every shard in parallel amortizes the network round trip.
A Targeted Query includes the shard key but still queries all shards to double-check for stale routing table entries, while Scatter-Gather queries skip that verification step.

explanation: Specification answer: Targeted queries include the Shard Key and route to exactly 1 shard; Scatter-Gather queries lack the shard key and broadcast to every shard in the cluster.

question: What does the $unwind stage do to an embedded array? What does the $unwind stage do to an embedded array?

options.text: It deconstructs an array field, outputting one document for every element in the array.
It merges every element of an array field into a single concatenated string, replacing the array with one scalar value per document.
It removes the array field from each document entirely, keeping the rest of the document unchanged and discarding the array's contents.
It groups documents by the values found in an array field, producing one output document per distinct array value across the whole collection rather than per source document.

explanation: Specification answer: It deconstructs an array field, outputting one document for every element in the array.

question:
During triage in MongoDB Aggregations Replicas Sharding, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: Cluster-Wide Scatter-Gather Latency Spikes on Sharded MongoDB".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: High-frequency operational user profile queries filter on email instead of the collection shard key tenantid, broadcasting every query to all 10 shards.
The collection is sharded on tenant_id using a hashed shard key, and hashed sharding always requires a scatter-gather for every query regardless of which fields are filtered.

mongos caches an outdated routing table after a chunk migration, so even queries that do include tenant_id are routed to the wrong single shard and return zero results, forcing an application-level retry across all shards.
The email field has a unique index defined on it, and mongos always scatter-gathers any query that touches a uniquely-indexed field to enforce the uniqueness constraint at query time.

explanation:
Root Cause: High-frequency operational user profile queries filter on email instead of the collection shard key tenantid, broadcasting every query to all 10 shards.

Fix Resolution:
Include the shard key in the query filter: db.users.find({'tenantid': tenant, 'email': email}).
